Question B-006-004-002.

Why the correct answer is right: Open-wire line has very low loss when installed correctly. It can tolerate high standing wave ratio (SWR) with less heating than many coax runs, which is why it is often used with tuners on multiband high-frequency (HF) antennas.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It can be located near metal objects without problems": Balanced open-wire line is especially sensitive to nearby metal because its fields are outside the conductors.
- sourceIndex 2: "It has low impedance, which facilitates matching to a transceiver": Open-wire line is usually relatively high impedance, not a low-impedance direct match to a 50-ohm transceiver.
- sourceIndex 3: "It does not radiate RF energy, which could cause interference to nearby equipment": A well-balanced line minimizes radiation, but poor routing or imbalance can still make it radiate.
